fields.description: The cluster the user sees. One Atlas = one region.
fields.label: Region

fields.description: Base URL of the regional Atlas, e.g. https://blr.atlas.example.com
fields.label: Base URL

fields.description: Atlas admin API key. Central authenticates with the Atlas admin token for every Central→Atlas call (the registration handshake and, once Active, the data path over the tunnel).
fields.label: Admin API Key

fields.description: Atlas admin API secret, paired with the key (stored encrypted).
fields.label: Admin API Secret

fields.description: How the console presents this region — the map pin and region labels. Maintained by the operator for now; Atlas becomes the source of truth for these once it reports region metadata.
fields.label: Display

fields.description: Human region label shown in the console, e.g. Mumbai, India.
fields.label: Display Name

fields.description: Infrastructure provider hosting this region, shown as the pin's brand mark. Unknown providers fall back to a monogram in the console.
fields.label: Provider

fields.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g. IN. The console derives the flag emoji from it.
fields.label: Country Code

fields.description: Region latitude for the console's world map. Leave empty to keep the region off the map (it still lists normally).
fields.label: Latitude

fields.description: Region longitude for the console's world map.
fields.label: Longitude

fields.description: The Central-managed WireGuard tunnel. Every field here is set by Register — not hand-entered.
fields.label: Tunnel

fields.description: Local development only: register without a WireGuard tunnel. Central does the identity half (scoped service user, pushed creds) and leaves the data path on the public base_url. No hub peering, no firewall lockdown.
fields.label: Skip Tunnel (Local Dev)

fields.description: Unregistered → Provisioning (wg0 up, firewall armed) → Active (confirmed over the tunnel). Inactive = still registered (keeps the service user) but the tunnel has been stripped down; Register again to bring it back up.
fields.label: Tunnel Status

fields.description: This Atlas's /32 on wg0, allocated from the pool, e.g. 10.88.0.2. Unique — the hard backstop against a double-allocation race.
fields.label: Tunnel IP

fields.description: Derived from tunnel_ip (e.g. https://10.88.0.2). The post-registration data path; base_url is used only during bootstrap.
fields.label: Tunnel URL

fields.description: The per-Atlas scoped Central service user this Atlas authenticates as when it reports events.
fields.label: Service User

fields.description: The Atlas's WireGuard public key, returned by provision_tunnel and added to the hub as a peer.
fields.label: Peer Public Key

fields.description: The Atlas's public wg endpoint (host of base_url : listen port) the hub dials.
fields.label: Peer Endpoint

fields.description: Result of the last Test Connection (over the current data path — base_url before/after the tunnel, tunnel_url while Active).
fields.label: Reachable
